PASS: QA1 static audit, sprint 3, round 2. Verdict PASS.
Audited commit ffe1389, tree 62a67a3a48f9de55bde7672221242da4feb86a8b, working tree clean.
Sprint file re-read IN FULL, fresh, immediately before recording -- it changed this round
(Amendment 2 added requirements 13-15), hash
bce74e68e0774327cf277848488f6e71b4e5d13e65a554601df6d5f8aaff9ef9.

ALL FOUR ROUND-1 FINDINGS FIXED.

1. Step 1 generic message -- FIXED. goToStep2 now accumulates the missing fields and
   reports "Missing: employment status, length of employment." Requirement 6 satisfied at
   step 1, which was the one place it slipped.
2. Empty strings in Situation.facts -- FIXED, and fixed better than I proposed. I suggested
   filtering the empties. Amendment 2 requirement 14 went the other way and kept all three
   entries while making the distinction type-level, which is the correct call: filtering
   would have destroyed exactly the information Sprint 5 needs. My round-1 recommendation
   is superseded and the superseding design is better.
3. Silent return on submit -- FIXED. The unreachable-guard branch now sets an explicit
   message pointing back to steps 1 and 2, with a comment recording why it is currently
   unreachable and why it is surfaced anyway (Sprint 7 step-jumping/resume). Exactly the
   fix requested.
4. Non-empty tuple defeated by a cast -- FIXED. `as [ConcernCategory, ...]` is gone;
   `const [firstConcern, ...restConcerns] = concerns` then `[firstConcern, ...restConcerns]`
   infers the tuple type structurally. No assertion remains on that path.

AMENDMENT 2 -- ALL THREE REQUIREMENTS MET.

Req 13 (per-prompt validation): three named exported constants --
  MIN_WHAT_HAPPENED_LENGTH 100, MIN_DOCUMENTATION_LENGTH 20, MIN_EMPLOYER_ACTION_LENGTH 20 --
  each with a comment giving a real rationale, not a restatement. The differentiated values
  are reasoned rather than uniform: the documentation prompt is often a short specific fact
  ("A doctor's note was requested and provided on March 3") rather than a narrative, so a
  100-char bar there would push users toward padding. The combined gate is GONE, not
  supplemented -- grepped app/, components/ and lib/ for MIN_NARRATIVE_LENGTH and
  validateNarrative: zero hits.
  AC 110's specific test exists and passes (intake-validation.test.ts:39), named for the
  round-1 scenario: 100 chars in prompt one, other two empty -> prompt one valid, other two
  INVALID. The exact case the combined threshold let through.

Req 14 (type-level not-reported marker): FactPromptResponse is a genuine discriminated
  union -- { reported: true; text: string } | { reported: false }. An empty string cannot
  masquerade as "not applicable" and a not-reported entry cannot carry text; both are
  unrepresentable, not merely discouraged. Situation.facts is a fixed
  [FactPromptResponse, FactPromptResponse, FactPromptResponse] tuple -- always three, never
  filtered, positionally bound to requirement 4's three prompts. Sprint 5's three-state
  ProceduralCheckStatus is now reachable: "no documentation was exchanged" and "the employer
  skipped the question" are distinguishable, which was Amendment 2's stated reason for
  existing. toFactPromptResponse is unit-tested to return the marker with no `text` property
  at all, not an empty one.
  UI half present: a per-prompt "Nothing yet / not applicable" checkbox with its own label
  and id, disabling the textarea when checked.

Req 15 (ARIA on the validation path): role="alert" on every message container (3 sites),
  aria-describedby wiring inputs and fieldsets to their message ids (6 sites),
  aria-invalid on the failing inputs. Present across steps 1, 2 and 3, not just one.

EVERYTHING FROM ROUND 1 STILL HOLDS -- RE-VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
lib/types.ts changes remain bounded to requirements 10, 11 and 14. The only additions this
  round are FactPromptResponse and the Situation.facts retype, both requirement 14. No other
  domain type changed shape.
ConcernCategory 4 intake concerns / FactPatternTag 4 legal patterns, zero overlap (set
  intersection, not eye). HumanRightsCodeGround still 15.
data/seed-library.json, lib/seed-library.ts, lib/citation-guard.ts and both Sprint 2 test
  files are untouched across the ENTIRE sprint diff, not just this round. Loader and guard
  have no behavioural change of any kind.
seed-library-schema.ts unchanged since round 1, where I proved the Record<FactPatternTag,
  true> exhaustiveness check still fails to compile on an added fact pattern.
No locally declared domain type. The two local declarations are `type Step = 1|2|3` (UI
  state) and ValidationResult (a mechanism result shape, same class as Sprint 2's
  CitationGuardResult).
On AC 108's prohibition of utility-type aliases: intake-validation.ts:84 uses
  Extract<FactPromptResponse, { reported: true }> as an inline type predicate in a filter.
  This is not what that criterion forbids. It is derived from the domain type so it cannot
  drift, it names the union's own branch rather than a near-copy, and it never becomes a
  shape a component depends on -- it exists only to narrow inside toNarrative. Passes.
Suite 16/16 across 4 files. typecheck clean, lint clean.
Requirement 9's four original cases all still present and passing.

DOCUMENTATION DEFECT -- MASTER CONTROLLER CLEANUP, NOT A CODE FIX, NOT BLOCKING

Acceptance criterion line 117 still reads: "QA1 confirms the minimum-detail threshold is a
single named exported constant with an explanatory comment, not a magic number inline."
That directly contradicts AC line 110 ("three named exported constants ... and no single
combined gate remaining") and requirement 13 ("The single combined MIN_NARRATIVE_LENGTH gate
is replaced, not supplemented"). Line 117 is residue Amendment 2 forgot to strike.

I audited against requirement 13 and AC 110. Stating that explicitly because it is a
judgment about precedence, not a waiver: Amendment 2 is the later, explicit instruction and
says which way the conflict resolves, so satisfying AC 117 would require violating the
requirement written to replace it. This is not the Sprint 1 requirement-8 situation, where a
criterion was genuinely unsatisfiable with nothing superseding it and the resolution needed
a real decision. If Master Controller disagrees with my reading, the verdict changes.

Strike line 117. It matters beyond tidiness: this PASS freezes the sprint file hash with the
contradiction inside it, and Sprint 4 is the next sprint and a natural candidate for reusing
this file as a template. This is the third time an amendment has left a stale acceptance
criterion behind (Sprint 1 requirement 8, Sprint 1 AC 89, now this) -- worth a line in
CLAUDE.md's amendment guidance: an amendment that replaces a requirement must strike the
acceptance criteria that tested the old one, in the same edit.

HANDOFF WARNING
This PASS freezes the sprint file hash. /sprint-dev-done is the only command that checks it
and refuses outright if the file changed. Do not edit the sprint file -- including striking
AC 117 -- between now and /sprint-dev-done. Do it after /sprint-ship, per CLAUDE.md's timing
constraint, or before dev-done and re-run this audit.

CARRIED FORWARD FOR SPRINT 5
Situation.facts is now a positional 3-tuple of FactPromptResponse. Sprint 5's spotter must
handle `reported: false` as a distinct input state rather than treating it as absence, and
CodeGround.triggeredBy should never cite a non-reported prompt. That is the whole point of
requirement 14 and it is the first thing Sprint 5's audit should check.

VERDICT: PASS. Gate 1 clear. Dev Team may run /sprint-dev-done.

CHECKS (verbatim results + evidence)

[x] AC: complete all three steps with realistic input and confirm a Situation is
    produced -- PASS.
    Completed twice (once by mouse, once keyboard-only). The completion screen
    renders the captured Situation. Mouse run captured verbatim:
      Employment status: active
      Tenure: 4 years, 3 months
      Formal complaints lodged to date: No
      Concerns: medical-absence, schedule-flexibility
      Narrative: the "what happened" text, then the "employer action" text
    Concern values are the INTAKE vocabulary (medical-absence,
    schedule-flexibility), not legal fact patterns. Requirement 10's vocabulary
    split is observable in the shipped output, not just in the types.

[x] AC: navigate backward from step 3 to step 1, previously entered data still
    present -- PASS.
    From step 3, Back -> step 2: both concern checkboxes still checked
    (Medical / absence, Schedule flexibility), other two still unchecked.
    Back again -> step 1: employment status "Active" still selected, tenure
    still "4 years, 3 months", formal complaints still "No".
    Then forward again to step 3: the 224-character narrative was still intact.
    Retention holds in BOTH directions, not just backward.

[x] AC: proceed from step 2 with no concern selected, blocked with a specific
    message -- PASS.
    Stayed on "Step 2 of 3: Primary concern". Message verbatim:
      "Select at least one concern to continue."
    Delivered in a role="alert" container, with aria-describedby on the
    fieldset resolving to that live element (target confirmed to exist).

[x] AC: submit a two-word narrative, analysis does not run, message names what
    is missing -- PASS.
    Entered "Sick lots" (9 chars) in prompt 1, prompts 2 and 3 empty. Blocked on
    step 3, "Intake complete" never reached. Three messages, verbatim:
      "What happened: add more detail â€” at least 100 characters (currently 9),
       or mark "Nothing yet / not applicable"."
      "Documentation exchanged: add more detail â€” at least 20 characters
       (currently 0), or mark "Nothing yet / not applicable"."
      "Employer action: add more detail â€” at least 20 characters (currently 0),
       or mark "Nothing yet / not applicable"."
    Each names the prompt, its required minimum, the actual current count, and
    the alternative. Requirement 6's "no shaming" holds -- the wording is
    "add more detail", not a rebuke.

[x] AC: detailed answer to the first prompt only, other two blank, BLOCKED --
    PASS. This is the regression case Amendment 2 exists for, and it is the
    check I most wanted to see fail if the fix were cosmetic.
    Prompt 1: 224 characters (verified by reading the live textarea value).
    Prompts 2 and 3: 0 characters.
    Under the superseded combined 100-character gate this would have PASSED.
    Live result: BLOCKED, still on step 3, "Intake complete" not reached.
    Exactly TWO alerts fired -- documentation and employer action -- and
    prompt 1's own alert had cleared, since 224 >= its own 100 minimum. That is
    per-prompt evaluation behaving correctly, not a blanket refusal.

[x] AC: use "nothing yet / not applicable" on the documentation prompt, flow
    proceeds -- PASS.
    Checked the documentation prompt's checkbox. Its textarea immediately became
    disabled and its validation message cleared on the spot, leaving only the
    employer-action message. Filled prompt 3, submitted, reached "Intake
    complete".
    Notable and correct: the not-applicable prompt is OMITTED from the rendered
    narrative rather than contributing an empty line. Consistent with
    requirement 14's type-level distinction rather than an empty string standing
    in for "not reported".

[x] AC: complete the entire flow using only the keyboard -- PASS. Zero mouse
    clicks in this run, start to finish.
    Step 1: Tab to "Active" radio (visible focus ring confirmed), Space to
      select, Tab to tenure input, typed "2 years", Tab into the complaints
      group, ArrowRight to move to and select "No", Tab to Next, Enter.
    Step 2: Tab to "Medical / absence", Space, Tab x5 to Next, Enter.
    Step 3: Tab to prompt 1, typed; Tab x2 to prompt 2, typed; Tab x2 to
      prompt 3, typed (163 / 54 / 75 characters); Tab x3 to "Complete intake",
      Enter.
    Reached "Intake complete" with the Situation rendered.
    Requirement 8's label requirement verified programmatically via each
    element's .labels collection, not by eyeballing proximity:
      tenure input -> "Length of employment (tenure)"
      textarea 1   -> "What happened, and over what timeframe?"
      textarea 2   -> "What documentation or medical information has been exchanged?"
      textarea 3   -> "What action is the employer considering, if any?"

[x] AC: Sprint 1 disclaimer banner visible on every step -- PASS.
    Confirmed present at rectTop 0 on step 1, step 2, step 3, and the "Intake
    complete" screen, across both runs, plus on the blocked/error states.
    Text checked character-for-character on the completion screen: exact match,
    length 66, character at index 31 is code 8212 (U+2014 EM DASH).
    Computed position "sticky".
    Also confirmed in server-rendered HTML (first paint, before hydration) on
    "/", "/about" and "/intake", 2 runs each: exactly ONE rendered banner tag
    per document, "sticky top-0 z-50" present, HTTP 200 on all three.

NON-REGRESSION ON SPRINTS 1 AND 2
- "/" and "/about" still render the banner exactly once, first paint, sticky.
- Landing page now offers "Start intake" -> /intake alongside the existing
  "View the placeholder route" -> /about. Both routes still work.
- No Sprint 2 case content is user-visible anywhere: no BCHRT string and no
  "VERIFIED CASE CITATION NEEDED" in the server HTML of any route, nor in the
  rendered text of the completion screen. Sprint 2's scope boundary still holds
  now that a real UI exists to violate it.

ACCESSIBILITY OF THE VALIDATION PATH (requirement 15) -- STATED PRECISELY
Confirmed live on step 3: all three textareas carried aria-invalid="true" when
failing, each with aria-describedby pointing at its OWN message element, and
each message container had role="alert". Step 1's tenure input likewise carried
aria-invalid when the step was submitted empty.
One nuance I am recording rather than glossing: step 2's concern group does NOT
carry aria-invalid. It uses role="alert" plus aria-describedby on the fieldset.
I am not calling this a defect -- aria-invalid is not a valid attribute on a
fieldset, and there is no single failing input in a checkbox group -- but
requirement 15 says "aria-invalid on the failing input" without addressing the
group case, so "aria-invalid is present throughout" would be an overstatement.
It is present on every element where it is applicable.

ISSUES FOUND
None blocking.

OBSERVATION 1 [LOW, not a criterion, not blocking] -- focus is not managed
across step transitions. After pressing Enter on Next, document.activeElement
returns to BODY rather than moving to the new step's heading or first control.
The flow remains fully keyboard-operable -- one Tab from body reaches the first
control, which is how I completed the keyboard run -- so requirement 8 is met.
But a screen-reader user gets no announcement that the step changed, and on a
form whose subject matter is disability accommodation that is worth a look.
Recommend it to Master Controller as a small follow-up (move focus to the step
heading with tabindex="-1" on advance), not as a Sprint 3 blocker: no acceptance
criterion covers focus management and the criterion that does exist,
"keyboard-navigable end to end", genuinely passes.

OBSERVATION 2 [environmental, not the app] -- one console exception appeared
during the first (mouse-driven) run:
  "Error: A listener indicated an asynchronous response by returning true, but
   the message channel closed before a response was received"
reported against /intake:0:0 with no stack in application code. I did not
attribute this to the app on sight. Evidence it is the browser-extension layer:
it is the canonical Chrome extension message-passing error; it did NOT reproduce
on a fresh load of /intake; /about was clean on the same tab; and the ENTIRE
second run -- a full keyboard flow through all three steps to completion --
produced zero console messages. The app itself makes no async messaging calls.
Recording it because a console exception on a page under test should never go
unmentioned, and recording the attribution reasoning so nobody has to re-derive
it next round.

CONSISTENCY
The intake flow is deterministic -- no AI, no network, no persistence this
sprint. Repetition run where it could reveal something: the full flow completed
twice by two different input methods with consistent results, and server-HTML
first-paint checks run twice per route across three routes with identical
output. No flake.

CARRIED FORWARD
The sticky-banner scroll check from Sprints 1 and 2 is now genuinely
user-observable for the first time: step 3 is taller than the viewport and
scrolls naturally, and the banner stayed pinned at top 0 while I scrolled
through the three prompts. The "inject filler to force overflow" workaround is
no longer needed. Closing that carried-forward note.

VERDICT: PASS. Gate 2 clear.
Code ready. Not authorization to close -- /sprint-complete still requires the
user's explicit, real-time go-ahead via --user-said, and that is Dev Team's
command to run, not mine.
user_said=Yes, close Sprint 3. Both gates are green and the two non-blocking observations (focus management, environmental console noise) are deferred, not blockers.
